body: Couldn't reproduce this one. Can you try again or maybe download the Edge DevTools from the Windows Store and see if there's any console errors?

To be honest I don't think it is even getting as far as creating the webview, the devtools shows no instances to connect to (running the packaged build does show an instance to connect to).

I walked through the issue with @nothingismagick in chat but we couldn't fix the problem. 

I can also run the same repo on another machine without problem.
 
The version of Microsoft EdgeHTML is 18.19041 if that is of any help to narrow down the issue.

currently you need to execute your project dev process first manually and wait until it is listening on a port... then only do yarn tauri dev

i face the same problem with svelte+sapper+webpack project... the sapper dev is always slower to be ready than the tauri dev, so i need to remove beforeDevCommand and manually wait for the sapper dev to be ready, then only type the tauri dev
Did you face the same issue with tauri.js v0.9.0? @thienpow tauri should now wait for the devServer to be reachable.

I tried it both with a local dev server, and with direct access to the dist files (as suggested by nothingismagick), neither worked.

Also tried updating to the latest versions, no improvement.

I still think something is failing when it tries to instantiate the webview, but not sure how I can debug this.

Can you test using `yarn` instead of `npx`? We're finding some REALLY weird issues with `npx`.
Tried both, still no luck, is there any way to get more verbose logging when the webview is created ?

As I guessed it looks like the webview is at fault, I created a test https://github.com/obany/tauri-webview-test using just the original https://github.com/Boscop/web-view and that fails in the same way.

Edge mode fails, MSHTML works - so it is likely this issue https://github.com/Boscop/web-view/issues/96 and more specifically https://github.com/windows-toolkit/Microsoft.Toolkit.Win32/issues/50

https://github.com/Boscop/web-view/issues/96#issuecomment-568881215

(Are you running as administrator?)

Indeed that is the case, I was running from a Powershell shell in VSCode, which wasn't admin as far as I knew, but obviously it is.

Running below snippet returns True.
```
$user = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent();
(New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal $user).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltinRole]::Administrator)  
```

Where as a separate powershell instance returns False.

So finally up and running and able to connect with DevTools 🎉 

I would suggest and addendum to the docs, maybe with that PowerShell snippet to test.

Now if only I could use WebView2 with Edge Chromium support, so I don't have to worry so much about browser quirks 😉
Wow, we are definitely so far into the weeds here. And WTF why is VS Code running with administrator rights? That's something that everyone should know about.
"tauri info" should show that info then.
